description: The figure presents three pie charts comparing the distribution of four labeled categories (N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, N+K−) across difficulty levels labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard” under a “Zero-Shot” setting. Each pie chart contains 4 slices with percentage values printed inside the slices, and a legend on the right maps colors to labels: teal corresponds to N+K+, olive/yellow corresponds to N−K+, tan/brown corresponds to N−K−, and reddish-brown corresponds to N+K−. In the “easy” chart, the slices are approximately N+K+ (teal) 55.4%, N−K+ (olive) 38.3%, N−K− (tan) 4.6%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) 1.7%. In the “medium” chart, the slices are approximately N+K+ (teal) 58.8%, N−K+ (olive) 35.4%, N−K− (tan) 4.0%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) 1.8%. In the “hard” chart, the slices are approximately N−K− (tan) 37.9%, N−K+ (olive) 37.3%, N+K+ (teal) 18.1%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) 6.7%. No slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and the slice ordering varies by chart rather than following a consistent descending arrangement.
